lesson_title: Paper 2 Practice Run: Measurement and Maps at Examination Pace
hook_text: Feed the formula a diameter instead of a radius and your tank grows FOUR times too big.
clip_script: Paper 2 is the practical paper — a road, a classroom, a tank — and its marks sit on the crossings. Watch. The N3, Johannesburg to Durban, 568 kilometres at 100: that's 5,68 hours. NOT 5 hours 68 minutes — the decimal times sixty is about 41. The clock runs on sixties; that one conversion carries its own mark. Now the classroom: four walls, 84 square metres — minus the door and windows, 75,12 — times two coats, 150,24 — divided by 9 per litre, 16,69 litres. The shop sells 5-litre tins: 3,34 becomes FOUR tins, rounded UP, because three tins leaves bare wall and no one sells a third of a tin. Then times R649: R2 596. Measurement becomes quantity, quantity meets price — every exchange pays. The tank trap: the formula wants the RADIUS. Hand it the 1,1 metre diameter and your answer doesn't double — it QUADRUPLES, because the error gets squared. Halve first: 0,55, and the honest tank holds about 1 901 litres. And the crate: count whole boxes along each side — 4 by 4 by 3 is 48 — because volume division is only a ceiling, and part of a box ships nothing. Units on every line, times sixty, round up at the shop door. That's Paper 2, walked at exam pace.
visual_style: A highway strip map unrolling with a giant comma splitting 5,68 into hours and minutes; classroom walls unfolding flat like cardboard while areas subtract themselves; a tank inflating to absurd size then snapping back when the diameter halves; boxes clicking into a crate in a 4-by-4-by-3 grid.
pacing: Brisk highway opening, steady beat through the painting chain, dramatic pause on the quadrupling tank, crisp counted finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and take Paper 2's 150 marks one clean crossing at a time.
